API-BEN-001.scenario: Verify that the beneficiary list API returns a successful reply with paging details
API-BEN-001.preconditions: Admin is signed in to the console and has a valid access token.
steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/beneficiaries with page 0 and size 25, using the admin token.
Check the response status and the 'success' flag.
Check that the data part contains the list of records, the page number, the page size and the total count.
API-BEN-001.expected: The API answers 200 with success = true; the data has the record list, page number 0, page size 25 and the total number of beneficiaries.

API-BEN-002.scenario: Verify that each beneficiary in the list carries the fields the screen needs, with valid status values
API-BEN-002.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. At least one beneficiary exists on UAT (otherwise the test is skipped).
steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/beneficiaries (page 0, size 25).
Take the first beneficiary in the list.
Check that it has: reference, code, name, status, registration status and created date.
Check the status and registration status values.
API-BEN-002.test_data: Allowed status: PENDING, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, BLOCKED, REJECTED. Allowed registration status: NOT_REGISTERED, PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED, REJECTED
API-BEN-002.expected: All six fields are present and both status values are from the allowed lists.

API-BEN-003.scenario: Verify that opening a beneficiary by its reference returns the same beneficiary with its extra details
API-BEN-003.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. At least one beneficiary exists on UAT.
steps: Get the list of beneficiaries and note the reference and code of the first one.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/beneficiaries/<reference>.
Compare the reference and code with the list values.
Check that the attempt count and last-updated date are present.
API-BEN-003.test_data: Reference of the first beneficiary in the list
API-BEN-003.expected: The API answers 200; the reference and code match the list, and the attempt count and updated date are shown.

API-BEN-004.scenario: Verify that searching by beneficiary code returns that beneficiary
API-BEN-004.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. At least one beneficiary exists on UAT.
steps: Get the list of beneficiaries and note the code of the first one.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/beneficiaries with search = that code.
Look for the code in the returned records.
API-BEN-004.test_data: search: code of the first beneficiary in the list
API-BEN-004.expected: The API answers 200 and the searched beneficiary is in the results.

API-BEN-005.scenario: Verify that the system issues beneficiary codes in the correct format and never repeats one
API-BEN-005.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries/code five times in a row.
Note the code returned each time.
Check each code's format and compare all five codes.
API-BEN-005.test_data: 5 requests. Valid code format: 1 to 50 letters, digits, '_' or '-'
API-BEN-005.expected: Each request answers 200; all five codes are in the valid format and all five are different.

API-BEN-006.scenario: Check that a newly issued beneficiary code is not already used by an existing beneficiary
API-BEN-006.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries/code and note the new code.
Search the beneficiary list for that code.
API-BEN-006.expected: No existing beneficiary has the newly issued code.

API-BEN-007.scenario: Check that asking for a beneficiary with an unknown reference returns 'not found'
API-BEN-007.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/beneficiaries/<unknown reference>.
Read the response status and error code.
API-BEN-007.expected: The API answers 404 with error code NOT_FOUND.

API-BEN-008.scenario: Check that badly formed or harmful references are refused cleanly without a server error
API-BEN-008.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/beneficiaries/<reference> using each bad reference in turn.
Read the response status each time.
API-BEN-008.expected: Each request gets a 4xx answer (request refused); none gives a 5xx server error.

API-BEN-009.scenario: Check that 'Check status' and 'Block/Unblock' on an unknown beneficiary return 'not found'
API-BEN-009.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries/<unknown reference>/enquiry with an empty body.
Send a PATCH request to /api/v1/beneficiaries/<unknown reference>/toggle-status with an empty body.
Read the response status of each.

API-BEN-010.scenario: Check that creating a beneficiary with an empty body is refused and all mandatory fields are named
API-BEN-010.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries with an empty body {}.
Read the response status, error code and the list of field errors.
API-BEN-010.expected: The API answers 400 or 422 with code VALIDATION_ERROR; the errors name all five mandatory fields (code, name, account number, IFSC, email) and do not list the optional mobile number. Nothing is created.

API-BEN-011.scenario: Check that creating a beneficiary without any one mandatory field is refused
API-BEN-011.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Get a fresh beneficiary code from POST /api/v1/beneficiaries/code.
Build a valid beneficiary body with that code, then remove one mandatory field.
Send it as a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries.
Read the response status and field errors.
Repeat for each mandatory field.
API-BEN-011.test_data: Field removed (one at a time): beneficiary code, account number, email, IFSC, name. Other fields valid (name 'QA Auto ...', real IFSC, test email, 10-digit mobile)
API-BEN-011.expected: Each request is refused with 400 or 422 and the missing field is named in the errors; no beneficiary is created.

API-BEN-012.scenario: Check that an empty, spaces-only or null value in any mandatory field is refused
API-BEN-012.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Get a fresh beneficiary code from POST /api/v1/beneficiaries/code.
Build a valid beneficiary body and set one mandatory field to a blank value.
Send it as a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries.
Read the response status and field errors.
Repeat for every mandatory field and every blank value.
API-BEN-012.test_data: Fields: code, account number, email, IFSC, name. Blank values: '' (empty), '   ' (spaces only), null. 15 combinations
API-BEN-012.expected: Each request is refused with 400 or 422 and the blank field is named in the errors; no beneficiary is created.

API-BEN-013.scenario: Verify that the server itself (not only the screen) rejects invalid values for each beneficiary field
API-BEN-013.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Get a fresh beneficiary code from POST /api/v1/beneficiaries/code.
Build a valid beneficiary body and replace one field with an invalid value.
Send it as a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries.
Read the response status and field errors.
Repeat for every invalid value.
API-BEN-013.test_data: Account: '12345678' (8 digits), 19 digits, '5010abc0123456' (letters), '5010-0123-4567' (dashes), '50100 1234567' (space), '-123456789' (negative). IFSC: 'HDFC000123' (10 chars), 'HDFC00012345' (12 chars), 'HDFC1001234' (5th char not 0), '1234567890A' (digits first), 'HDFC0-01234' (symbol). Email: 'abc', 'abc@x', 'a b@x.com', 'abc@@x.com'. Mobile: '98765', '98765432101', 'abcdefghij', '+919876543210'. Name: 300 'A's. Code: 'EX CODE 01' (spaces), 51 'X's, 'EX<001>' (symbols)
API-BEN-013.expected: Every invalid value is refused with 400 or 422 and the bad field is named in the errors; no beneficiary is created and there is no server error.

API-BEN-014.scenario: Check that values of the wrong type (list, object, true/false) are refused cleanly without a server error
API-BEN-014.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Get a fresh beneficiary code and build a valid beneficiary body.
Replace one field with a value of the wrong type.
Send it as a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries and read the status.
Repeat for each variant.
API-BEN-014.test_data: 1) name as a list ['QA']  2) email as an object {"a": 1}  3) account number as true  4) IFSC as a list ['SBIN0000001']
API-BEN-014.expected: Each request is refused with a 4xx status (not 200/201 and not 5xx); nothing is created.

API-BEN-015.scenario: Check that a broken (malformed) JSON body is refused with a client error, not a server error
API-BEN-015.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/beneficiaries with content type JSON and an incomplete JSON body.
Read the response status.
API-BEN-015.expected: The API answers with a 4xx status (e.g. 400), never a 5xx server error.

API-BEN-020.sub_module: Create Beneficiary API – create and duplicate code
API-BEN-020.scenario: Verify that a beneficiary with only mandatory fields is created with a masked account, a repeat of the same request returns the same beneficiary, and reusing its code for another payee is refused
API-BEN-020.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. Note: this test creates one 'QA Auto' beneficiary on UAT.
steps: Get a fresh beneficiary code from POST /api/v1/beneficiaries/code.
Send POST /api/v1/beneficiaries with only the mandatory fields (code, name, account, IFSC, email) and no mobile.
Check the reply: same code, account number masked showing only the last 4 digits, and the full account number not present anywhere.
Open the beneficiary detail by its reference and check name, IFSC, email, empty mobile and masked account.
Send exactly the same create request again (as a retry after a timeout) and check the same beneficiary reference comes back.
Send a create request for a different payee using the same code.
Search the list by the code and count the matches.
API-BEN-020.test_data: Fresh code; name 'QA Auto <first> <last>'; valid account number; real IFSC; test email; no mobile
API-BEN-020.expected: First create answers 200/201 with the account masked. Detail matches what was sent, with no mobile and a masked account. The repeat returns the same beneficiary (nothing new). The different payee with the same code is refused (400/409/422) with code DUPLICATE_REFERENCE. Exactly one beneficiary carries the code.

API-BEN-021.scenario: Check that an existing beneficiary's code cannot be used to register a new payee
API-BEN-021.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. At least one beneficiary exists on UAT.
steps: Get the list of beneficiaries; note the code of the first one and the total count.
Send POST /api/v1/beneficiaries for a new payee using that existing code.
Read the response status and error code.
Get the list again and compare the total count.
API-BEN-021.test_data: Code: code of the first existing beneficiary; other fields: new valid payee details
API-BEN-021.expected: The API refuses with 400, 409 or 422 and code DUPLICATE_REFERENCE; the total number of beneficiaries is unchanged.

API-BEN-022.scenario: Check that a lower-case or space-padded copy of an existing code cannot create a look-alike payee
API-BEN-022.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. At least one beneficiary exists on UAT (the lower-case variant is skipped if the code has no letters).
steps: Get the code of the first existing beneficiary.
Make a variant of that code (lower case, or with spaces before and after).
Send POST /api/v1/beneficiaries for a new payee using the variant code.
Read the response status.
API-BEN-022.test_data: 1) existing code in lower case  2) existing code with two spaces before and after
API-BEN-022.expected: Each request is refused with 400, 409 or 422 (as duplicate or invalid); no new beneficiary is created.

API-BEN-023.scenario: Check that the same bank account and IFSC cannot be registered twice under different codes
API-BEN-023.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. Note: this test creates one 'QA Auto' beneficiary on UAT.
steps: Get a fresh code and register a valid beneficiary (first registration).
Get a second fresh code.
Send POST /api/v1/beneficiaries with the second code but the same account number and IFSC as the first.
Read the response status.
API-BEN-023.test_data: Second request: new code, new name/email, same account number and IFSC as the first beneficiary
API-BEN-023.expected: The first registration succeeds; the second is refused with 400, 409 or 422 (same payee twice).

API-BEN-030.scenario: Check that every beneficiary endpoint refuses a call made without a login token
API-BEN-030.preconditions: None (requests are sent without any token).
steps: Send each beneficiary request below without an Authorization header.
Read the response status and error code each time.
API-BEN-030.test_data: 1) GET /api/v1/beneficiaries (list)  2) GET /api/v1/beneficiaries/<unknown ref> (detail)  3) POST /api/v1/beneficiaries (create)  4) POST /api/v1/beneficiaries/code (issue code)  5) POST /api/v1/beneficiaries/<unknown ref>/enquiry  6) PATCH /api/v1/beneficiaries/<unknown ref>/toggle-status
API-BEN-030.expected: Every request answers 401 with code UNAUTHORIZED.

API-BEN-031.scenario: Check that fake, empty or wrong-type credentials are rejected
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries with each bad Authorization header below.
Read the response status each time.
API-BEN-031.test_data: 1) 'Bearer abc.def.ghi' (made-up token)  2) 'Bearer ' (empty)  3) Basic username/password header  4) 'Bearer null'

API-BEN-032.scenario: Check that a real login token with an altered signature is rejected
API-BEN-032.preconditions: Admin is signed in and a real access token is available.
steps: Take the admin's real access token and change the last two characters of its signature part.
Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries with the altered token.
Read the response status.
API-BEN-032.test_data: Admin token with the last 2 signature characters changed
API-BEN-032.expected: The API answers 401; the altered token is not accepted.

API-BEN-033.scenario: Check that an unsigned token (algorithm 'none') carrying the real user details is rejected
API-BEN-033.preconditions: Admin is signed in and a real access token is available.
steps: Build a token with header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}, the real token's user details, and no signature.
Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries with this token.
Read the response status.
API-BEN-033.test_data: Unsigned token with the admin's real claims
API-BEN-033.expected: The API answers 401; the unsigned token is not accepted.

API-BEN-034.scenario: Verify that no full bank account number appears anywhere in the beneficiary list response
API-BEN-034.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries with page 0 and size 100.
Check the account number of every record.
Search the whole response text for an account number with 5 or more plain digits.
API-BEN-034.expected: Every account number is masked (e.g. ****1234) and no raw account number appears in the response.

API-BEN-035.scenario: Verify that the beneficiary detail response shows the account number masked
API-BEN-035.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. At least one beneficiary exists on UAT.
steps: Get the reference of the first beneficiary from the list.
Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries/<reference>.
Check the account number in the reply.
API-BEN-035.expected: The account number is empty or masked, showing only the last few digits.

API-BEN-036.scenario: Verify that the list and detail responses contain no password, OTP, PIN, CVV, secret or token fields
API-BEN-036.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. At least one beneficiary exists on UAT.
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries.
Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries/<reference of the first beneficiary>.
Search both responses for sensitive field names.
API-BEN-036.test_data: Field names looked for: password, otp, pin, cvv, secret, token, authorization
API-BEN-036.expected: None of the sensitive field names appears in either response.

API-BEN-037.scenario: Check that SQL injection text in the search box neither causes an error nor returns extra records
API-BEN-037.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries with search set to each SQL text below (page 0, size 25).
Read the status, check for database error words, and check the total count.
API-BEN-037.expected: No 5xx error and no 'sql' or 'syntax' text in the reply; if the reply is 200, it returns zero records.

API-BEN-038.scenario: Check that a beneficiary name containing script code or SQL is refused
API-BEN-038.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. A beneficiary is created only if the server wrongly accepts the name.
steps: Get a fresh code and build a valid beneficiary body.
Set the name to the harmful text.
Send POST /api/v1/beneficiaries and read the status and field errors.
Repeat for the second value.
API-BEN-038.expected: Each request is refused with 400 or 422 naming the name field, or 403 from the web firewall; nothing is created.

API-BEN-039.scenario: Check that a caller cannot set system-controlled fields (status, registration, reference, dates) when creating a beneficiary
API-BEN-039.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. Note: this test may create one 'QA Auto' beneficiary on UAT.
steps: Get a fresh code and build a valid beneficiary body.
Add extra fields that only the system should set (see test data).
Send POST /api/v1/beneficiaries.
If refused with 400/422, the test passes. If created, open the beneficiary detail.
Check the reference, bank reference, attempt count, created date and registration status.
API-BEN-039.test_data: status: ACTIVE, registrationStatus: SUCCESS, beneficiaryReference: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, bankReference: QA-FORGED, attemptCount: 99, createdAt: 2000-01-01
API-BEN-039.expected: Either the request is refused (400/422), or the beneficiary is created but none of the sent system values were used: different reference, no 'QA-FORGED' bank reference, attempt count not 99, created date not in 2000, and it is not marked SUCCESS without a bank message.

API-BEN-040.scenario: Check that beneficiaries cannot be deleted or overwritten using other HTTP methods
API-BEN-040.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token. At least one beneficiary exists on UAT.
steps: Get the reference of the first beneficiary.
Send each request below and read the status.
API-BEN-040.expected: Each request answers 403, 404, 405 or 501; nothing is deleted or changed.

API-BEN-041.scenario: Verify that the beneficiary API sends the required security headers and tells browsers not to cache the data
API-BEN-041.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries.
Check the response headers.
API-BEN-041.test_data: Headers checked: Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options = nosniff, X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control
API-BEN-041.expected: All the listed security headers are present and Cache-Control contains 'no-store'.

API-BEN-042.scenario: Check that the API does not allow requests from an unknown outside website
API-BEN-042.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries with the Origin header set to an outside website.
Check the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.
API-BEN-042.expected: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is neither '*' nor the outside website.

API-BEN-043.scenario: Check that a very large page size is capped or refused so all data cannot be pulled in one call
API-BEN-043.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries with page 0 and a very large size.
Read the status and, if 200, the page size in the reply.
Repeat for the second size.
API-BEN-043.expected: No 5xx error; if the reply is 200, the page size used is 100 or less.

API-BEN-044.scenario: Check that invalid page or size values are handled without a server error
API-BEN-044.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries with each invalid paging value.
Read the response status.
API-BEN-044.expected: Each request is refused (4xx) or corrected by the server; none gives a 5xx error.

API-BEN-045.scenario: Verify that asking for many beneficiary codes quickly does not cause errors
API-BEN-045.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send POST /api/v1/beneficiaries/code 20 times quickly.
Read each response status.
API-BEN-045.expected: Every request answers 200, or 429 (too many requests) if a rate limit applies; no other status.

API-BEN-046.scenario: Check that each security header is sent only once (not doubled)
API-BEN-046.preconditions: Admin has a valid access token.
steps: Send GET /api/v1/beneficiaries.
Check that each security header has a single value (no comma-joined repeats such as 'DENY, DENY').
Check the Content-Security-Policy is not given twice.
API-BEN-046.test_data: Headers: X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy
API-BEN-046.expected: Each header appears with one value only, and only one Content-Security-Policy is sent.
